title: Prepare initial system
action: Generate LAMMPS data files for a system of two muscovite mica slabs (10×6×1 unit cells) with innermost K+ ions removed, 200 DDAB molecules, and 8000 water molecules, representing a 39.1 wt% DDAB solution. Use PCFF-INTERFACE force field parameters and random initial positions for surfactant and water.
description: Build the initial simulation cell using the mica structure from the Interface Force Field toolkit.

title: Run molecular dynamics simulation
action: Using LAMMPS, perform energy minimization, followed by NVE relaxation for 0.2 ns, apply a fixed load corresponding to 1 atm on the top mica slab, and then run NVT production at 298 K for 50 ns with a 1 fs timestep. Save trajectory for analysis.
description: Execute the full MD simulation protocol to obtain an equilibrated trajectory of the system without surface K+ ions.

title: Compute DDAB bilayer thickness and orientation distribution
action: From the last 20 ns of the trajectory, calculate atomic density profiles along z. Identify nitrogen atoms of DDAB headgroups near each surface. Determine average z-coordinates of the 'outer' layer (nitrogens closest to mica) and the 'inner' layer (nitrogens facing bulk) for each surface. Compute bilayer thickness L as the difference between these averages. Additionally, for each DDAB molecule, define a unit vector from the terminal N atom to the terminal methyl C atom for each of its two chains, compute cosθ with the laboratory z-axis, and bin all cosθ values into 10 equal bins between -1 and 1. Write a JSON object with keys 'top_L', 'bottom_L' (in Å), and 'orientation' (an object with keys 'bins' as a list of 11 bin-edge floats and 'counts' as a list of 10 integer counts) to /app/outputs/bilayer_thickness.json.
description: DDAB bilayer thickness on top and bottom mica surfaces, and molecular orientation distribution histogram
